texts.preamble: Madhav Mandal And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 2 January, 2024 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:136 Court No. - 84 Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 4361 of 2022 Appellant :- Madhav Mandal And 2 Others Respondent :- State of U.P. Counsel for Appellant :- Anand Kumar Singh,Roshni Murad,Suraj Kumar Singh
texts.arguments: 4. It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellants-applicants that the appellants are innocent and have falsely been implicated. It has been further submitted that the conviction and sentence imposed by the learned trial Judge is against the weight of evidence on record. The trial court has misread the evidence on record and convicted the appellants. The prosecution has not been able to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. It has been further submitted that the appellants were on bail during trial and have not misused the liberty of bail. Since there is no likelihood of early hearing of the appeal in near future, the appellants may be released on bail pending appeal. Besides the above submissions, learned counsel for the appellants has also tried to touch upon at length the circumstances which led to the false implication of accused - appellants. 5. Learned counsel for the appellants has further submitted that the impugned judgment and order has been passed without appreciating the material evidence on record. It is further submitted that the Nayab Tehsildar, Bharat Paswan, who was leading the team at the time of abolishing Thai Mangur has not been examined during trial who was the material witness. It is next submitted that perfect examination has not been performed during the investigation of this case in respect of thai mangur which is to be resulted hazardous for human health and ecosystem. It is also submitted that the relevant provision of Food Safety Standard Act has also not been promulgated by the trial court in proper manner. It is next submitted that the appellants have no criminal antecedents to their credit nor anything to this effect has been brought into light by the learned A.G.A. in the counter affidavit. It is next submitted that the appellants are languishing in jail since 30.05.2022. 6. On the other hand, learned AGA vehemently opposed the bail application but however he could not dispute the factual aspect of the matter as submitted by the learned counsel for the appellants.
